admission.justification: The shared Order/ready rendering in orderGraph.tsx and placement in taskReader.tsx jointly keep the master’s visible order and next-task list tied to the projected dependency frontier.

applicability: Dashboard ordinary-master Order and Now blocks composed from the master’s derived task graph.
conditions: Order follows Now and uses the drawing shared with sprint Order.
Entry stage/activity and the shared status table distinguish task work, while graph readiness stays a separate dependency fact. Each paused started graph unit remains once in its dependency wave.
Task counts/progress use the shared entry population; the separate graph-derived done/abandoned totals are removed.
Now lists graph-ready tasks whose native entry is planned; pointer rest retains both dependency directions and shared fade behavior.
exclusions: Changing the sprint executionGraph authoring contract.
Treating displayed readiness as a tool-enforced start decision.

evidence: Parent examination of actual F01 changed extents; no new execution or acceptance.

statement: Master pages reuse the sprint Order drawing after Now, with task-entry state/activity and producer dependency waves/readiness, both dependency directions on pointer rest, and graph-ready planned tasks listed as Can start next in Now. Completed/aborted membership and task progress come from the shared entries; Order adds no independent done/abandoned graph totals.
